title: Adversative connectors
schema: english-prompt -> learner types German -> Reveal/Hide answer shows reference + speaker

exercises.english: The report was long, but nobody read it anyway.
exercises.german: Der Bericht war lang, trotzdem hat ihn niemand gelesen.
exercises.why: trotzdem stands in slot II before the finite verb hat and cancels the expected effect of the concession.

exercises.english: The warning came in time, yet we set off all the same.
exercises.german: Die Warnung kam rechtzeitig, dennoch sind wir losgefahren.
exercises.why: dennoch is the more formal variant of trotzdem and also occupies field II.

exercises.english: He has a lot of experience, but he lacks the courage.
exercises.german: Er hat viel Erfahrung, allerdings fehlt ihm der Mut.
exercises.why: allerdings is a particle that prefers field I, but it is also used in field II, and here it limits a positive statement.

exercises.english: She is helpful in principle, but she is terrible at remembering names.
exercises.german: Sie ist grundsätzlich hilfsbereit, dabei merkt sie sich Namen schlecht.
exercises.why: dabei points back to something already known and can stand in field II as a contrastive adverb.

exercises.english: He was not rude, rather he was simply in a hurry.
exercises.german: Er war nicht unhöflich, vielmehr war er nur in Eile.
exercises.why: vielmehr in field II refuses a previously mentioned quality and substitutes a different one.

exercises.english: She did not resign, rather she took a paid year off.
exercises.german: Sie hat nicht gekündigt, vielmehr hat sie ein bezahltes Jahr genommen.
exercises.why: vielmehr can also be used with perfect-tense main clauses, and it corrects the expectation the negated clause created.

exercises.english: The contract is running out, yet nobody is renewing it.
exercises.german: Der Vertrag läuft aus, dennoch verlängert ihn niemand.
exercises.why: dennoch in field II forms a close contrast with a passive main clause.

exercises.english: In spite of all our efforts we are getting nowhere.
exercises.german: Trotzdem aller Bemühungen kommen wir nicht weiter.
exercises.why: The genitive plural of the concession is governed by trotzdem, and the adverb still takes field II.

exercises.english: Despite his explanation the accusation still stands.
exercises.german: Trotzdem seiner Erklärung bleibt der Vorwurf stehen.
exercises.why: trotzdem with the dative of the person or thing conceded; the main clause keeps normal order.

exercises.english: In spite of the rain we went for a walk.
exercises.german: Trotzdem des Regens gingen wir spazieren.
exercises.why: trotzdem plus genitive is neutral in gender here, and the verb gingen is the second field element.

exercises.english: Despite his good upbringing he does not understand the rule.
exercises.german: Trotzdem seiner guten Erziehung versteht er die Regel nicht.
exercises.why: The dative form seiner follows trotzdem; the negated verb stays in field III because the negated element steht already fills a slot.

exercises.english: Despite several cancellations the course is still going ahead.
exercises.german: Trotzdem mehrerer Absagen bleibt der Kurs geplant.
exercises.why: mehrerer is a genitive quantifier that has to agree with the plural Absagen.

exercises.english: Despite his request we are travelling without him.
exercises.german: Trotzdem seiner Bitte fahren wir ohne ihn.
exercises.why: A common error would be trotzdem die Bitte; the pronoun must stay in the dative.

exercises.english: Despite the low prices nobody is buying anything.
exercises.german: Trotzdem günstiger Preise kauft niemand ein.
exercises.why: günstiger Preise shows the uninflected adjective form used in a fixed genitive phrase.

exercises.english: The exercise is hard, but it will be worth it.
exercises.german: Die Übung fällt schwer, allerdings wird sie sich lohnen.
exercises.why: Here allerdings concedes a difficulty and then points to a compensation in field II.

exercises.english: Sales here are stagnating, whereas demand abroad is growing.
exercises.german: Der Absatz stagniert, hingegen wächst die Nachfrage im Ausland.
exercises.why: hingegen compares two clauses from different points of view and never stands in field I.

exercises.english: We are saving on materials, whereas staff costs are rising.
exercises.german: Wir sparen beim Material, hingegen steigen die Personalkosten.
exercises.why: A third-person verb in the following clause shows that hingegen sits in field II, not field I.

exercises.english: She is staying at home, whereas he works in the office.
exercises.german: Sie bleibt zu Hause, hingegen arbeitet er im Büro.
exercises.why: The change of subject makes the contrast explicit without any conjunction.

exercises.english: He only reads newspapers, whereas she is working through a whole stack of novels.
exercises.german: Er liest nur Zeitungen, sie hingegen einen ganzen Stapel Romane.
exercises.why: When the second subject is repeated, the verb and even objects may be left out after hingegen.

exercises.english: The software is mature, yet there is not a line of documentation.
exercises.german: Die Software ist ausgereift, dabei fehlt jede Dokumentation.
exercises.why: dabei in field II picks up the immediately preceding point and negates the expectation it created.

exercises.english: While he was talking about getting better, he looked completely exhausted.
exercises.german: Während er von der Erholung sprach, wirkte er völlig erschöpft.
exercises.why: The two states contradict each other, which is what makes this a contrastive and not a merely temporal während.

exercises.english: While the advertisement promised a quick solution, the repair took weeks.
exercises.german: Während die Anzeige eine schnelle Lösung versprach, dauerte die Reparatur Wochen.
exercises.why: The verb pair versprach and dauerte highlights the contradiction between promise and reality.

exercises.english: While she painted the walls, the neighbours argued the whole time.
exercises.german: Während sie die Wände strich, stritten die Nachbarn die ganze Zeit.
exercises.why: This is the temporal reading: zwei Vorgänge laufen gleichzeitig ab, one positive, one unwelcome.

exercises.english: While I was waiting for the letter, the postman walked past our house.
exercises.german: Während ich auf den Brief wartete, ging der Postbote an unserem Haus vorbei.
exercises.why: Simultaneity alone: the waiting and the passing are neutral, so the clause is temporal, not contrastive.

exercises.english: While she claims to be short of time, she always finds an hour for the gym.
exercises.german: Während sie behauptet, keine Zeit zu haben, findet sie immer eine Stunde fürs Training.
exercises.why: The two statements are incompatible, so während introduces an ironic contrast.

exercises.english: While he apologised for the delay, he did not mention the reason.
exercises.german: Während er sich für die Verspätung entschuldigte, nannte er keinen Grund.
exercises.why: The contrast lies between the apology and the missing explanation, marked by keinen Grund.

exercises.english: While they praised the project, half the team left before the end.
exercises.german: Während sie das Projekt lobten, verließ die halbe Mannschaft vor dem Schluss.
exercises.why: Public praise and the mass departure form the paradox that während highlights.

exercises.english: While the doctor forbade him sport, he ran a half-marathon.
exercises.german: Während der Arzt ihm Sport verbot, lief er einen Halbmarathon.
exercises.why: Temporal setting with a clear contradiction; a single temporal reading would be neutral, the verb contrast carries the irony.

exercises.english: While the rent is rising, the number of tenants is falling.
exercises.german: Während die Miete steigt, sinkt die Zahl der Mieter.
exercises.why: Two simultaneous developments in opposite directions, the classic economic contrast.

exercises.english: While we were queuing for tickets, they were already giving them away.
exercises.german: Während wir für Karten anstanden, verschenkten sie welche.
exercises.why: The queue and the free give-away are simultaneous opposites in the same scene.

exercises.english: While the report praises the plant, the staff consider it a firetrap.
exercises.german: Während der Bericht die Anlage lobt, halten die Beschäftigten sie für eine Brandfalle.
exercises.why: Official report and insider opinion contradict each other; both clauses stay in the present for a general contrast.

exercises.english: While she was packing, her brother unpacked the bags again.
exercises.german: Während sie die Koffer packte, packte ihr Bruder sie wieder aus.
exercises.why: Contradictory parallel actions make this contrastive even though the timing is simultaneous.

exercises.english: While he promised to get in touch, he disappeared for a week.
exercises.german: Während er zusagte, sich zu melden, verschwand er für eine Woche.
exercises.why: The promise and the disappearance clash, so the clause works as a contrastive rather than merely temporal setting.

exercises.english: While the workshop was full of praise for the design, nobody mentioned the cost.
exercises.german: Während die Werkstatt den Entwurf lobte, erwähnte niemand die Kosten.
exercises.why: Praise plus silence about the price is the contrast the sentence stages.

exercises.english: While the audience clapped, the soloist made a false note.
exercises.german: Während das Publikum klatschte, sang die Solistin einen falschen Ton.
exercises.why: Apparent success and the audible error contradict each other.

exercises.english: While everybody was searching for the key, it lay in her pocket.
exercises.german: Während alle nach dem Schlüssel suchten, lag er in ihrer Tasche.
exercises.why: The search and the obvious place are simultaneous opposites with an ironic point.

exercises.english: While the company saves on staff, it spends a fortune on consultants.
exercises.german: Während die Firma beim Personal spart, gibt sie für Berater ein Vermögen aus.
exercises.why: Two simultaneous but contradictory decisions make the contrast unmistakable.

exercises.english: While he was signing the contract, his old car broke down outside.
exercises.german: Während er den Vertrag unterschrieb, blieb sein alter Wagen draußen liegen.
exercises.why: Purely temporal: the main clause narrates what happened at the same moment, no contradiction.

exercises.english: While she insists on early flights, she never gets up before nine.
exercises.german: Während sie auf frühe Flüge besteht, steht sie nie vor neun auf.
exercises.why: Insistence and behaviour contradict each other, giving the ironic contrastive reading.

exercises.english: While they said the software was stable, it crashed three times on Monday.
exercises.german: Während sie behaupteten, die Software sei stabil, stürzte sie am Montag dreimal ab.
exercises.why: Claim and event clash; the finite verb in the subordinate clause brackets the reported statement.

exercises.english: He is not in Berlin, he is in Hamburg.
exercises.german: Er ist nicht in Berlin, sondern in Hamburg.
exercises.why: sondern stands in field III and replaces the negated member of the same set.

exercises.english: She did not call, she wrote an email.
exercises.german: Sie hat nicht angerufen, sondern eine E-Mail geschrieben.
exercises.why: Perfect tense: the negation covers the auxiliary and the participle, sondern links the two clauses.

exercises.english: I did not go swimming, I went running.
exercises.german: Ich bin nicht schwimmen gegangen, sondern joggen.
exercises.why: The verb phrase after sondern is the elliptical form, with only the infinitival complement.

exercises.english: The problem is not the price but the delivery time.
exercises.german: Das Problem ist nicht der Preis, sondern die Lieferzeit.
exercises.why: A copula takes a nominal complement on both sides; the negated noun is the only member replaced.

exercises.english: We did not lose money, we broke even.
exercises.german: Wir haben kein Geld verloren, sondern nur die Kosten gedeckt.
exercises.why: Here the negated part is a noun, so the ellipsis after sondern is not a verb at all.

exercises.english: He is not tired but rather bored.
exercises.german: Er ist nicht müde, sondern gelangweilt.
exercises.why: Adjectives without sein stand in the first part, so the second part is reduced to the adjective.

exercises.english: They are not at school, they are on a school trip.
exercises.german: Sie sind nicht in der Schule, sondern auf Klassenfahrt.
exercises.why: Two locative complements are opposed; the prepositional phrase stands in the second position of the main clause.

exercises.english: I did not understand the question, I simply did not hear it.
exercises.german: Ich habe die Frage nicht verstanden, sondern einfach nicht gehört.
exercises.why: A near-synonym of the negated word appears in the second part, which sharpens the contrast.

exercises.english: It is not a question of money but of time.
exercises.german: Es ist keine Frage des Geldes, sondern der Zeit.
exercises.why: The genitive parallel after the preposition of must be repeated, nicht … sondern does not license ellipsis here.

exercises.english: She did not want to rest, she wanted to work.
exercises.german: Sie wollte sich nicht ausruhen, sondern arbeiten.
exercises.why: A verb second clause with the same subject follows, which is possible with the final sondern.

exercises.english: The wine is not red but white.
exercises.german: Der Wein ist nicht rot, sondern weiß.
exercises.why: The classic minimal pair: two predicative adjectives, one negated, one substituted.

exercises.english: I did not arrive late, I came in time.
exercises.german: Ich bin nicht zu spät gekommen, sondern pünktlich.
exercises.why: Adverbials replace each other; the negated adverb occupies the same slot the second adverb takes.

exercises.english: He is not out of spite, he is out of principle.
exercises.german: Er handelt nicht aus Bosheit, sondern aus Prinzip.
exercises.why: The second aus-phrase repeats the preposition but takes a new noun, showing no full ellipsis.

exercises.english: We did not lose the final, we were eliminated in the semi-final.
exercises.german: Wir haben das Finale nicht verloren, sondern erst im Halbfinale ausgeschieden.
exercises.why: A longer predicate replaces the negated one, so the second clause cannot be shortened further.

exercises.english: The film is not a thriller but a family drama.
exercises.german: Der Film ist kein Thriller, sondern ein Familiendrama.
exercises.why: Indefinite pronouns kein and ein are contrasted inside the same noun slot.

exercises.english: I am not angry, only disappointed.
exercises.german: Ich bin nicht ärgerlich, sondern enttäuscht.
exercises.why: Only the adjective changes; the copula and the subject are identical.

exercises.english: She is not only a colleague, but also the person we confide in.
exercises.german: Sie ist nicht nur Kollegin, sondern auch unsere Vertrauensperson.
exercises.why: sondern auch adds a role to the negated one; the focus stays on the first predicate.

exercises.english: The flat is not only quiet, but also centrally located.
exercises.german: Die Wohnung ist nicht nur ruhig, sondern auch zentral.
exercises.why: nur … auch coordinates two adjectives, so both properties are asserted.

exercises.english: He not only helped, but also paid for everything.
exercises.german: Er hat nicht nur geholfen, sondern auch alles bezahlt.
exercises.why: The second verb group replaces nothing, it enlarges what the first one did.

exercises.english: We not only waited, but also complained the whole time.
exercises.german: Wir haben nicht nur gewartet, sondern auch die ganze Zeit geschimpft.
exercises.why: sondern auch links two past actions, and the coordinated verb groups are both complete.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: The flat is expensive, but it does have three rooms.
exercises.german: Zwar ist die Wohnung teuer, drei Zimmer gibt es dafür.
exercises.why: zwar concedes the price, the second clause adds the compensating fact; no closing aber is needed when the contrast is loose.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: He is new, but his results are better.
exercises.german: Er ist zwar noch neu, seine Ergebnisse sind aber besser.
exercises.why: The two clauses are independent main clauses, which is the standard zwar … aber pattern.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: I was wrong, but the damage was small.
exercises.german: Zwar habe ich mich geirrt, doch der Schaden war gering.
exercises.why: With doch the main clause is inverted: the verb war comes before the subject der Schaden.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: All right, I was wrong.
exercises.german: Na gut, ich habe mich geirrt.
exercises.why: na gut concedes a point in a single short sentence, with no second clause at all.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: Admittedly the idea was good, only the execution was not.
exercises.german: Zugegeben, die Idee war gut, nur die Umsetzung nicht.
exercises.why: The bare form zugegeben opens the sentence, and nur closes the contrast.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: The date was awkward, but we kept it anyway.
exercises.german: Der Termin war zwar ungünstig, wir haben ihn trotzdem wahrgenommen.
exercises.why: zwar in field I, main clause with normal field II order.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: Well, that was not exactly a success.
exercises.german: Na ja, ein Erfolg war das nicht.
exercises.why: na ja concedes with visible scepticism; a following negation creates the contrast.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: I do not know how it will go on, but I am staying with it.
exercises.german: Zwar weiß ich nicht, wie es weitergeht, ich bleibe aber dabei.
exercises.why: zwar introduces the concession, aber carries the main message.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: She has a lot of experience, but she lacks patience.
exercises.german: Sie hat zwar viel Erfahrung, nur fehlt ihr die Geduld.
exercises.why: nur as the closing particle after a zwar clause, typical of spoken German.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: Admittedly one could have informed me.
exercises.german: Zugegebenermaßen hätte man mich informieren können.
exercises.why: A one-clause concession; the missing second part makes the reproach implicit.

exercises.english: He runs fast, he is not athletic.
exercises.german: Er läuft schnell, er ist nicht sportlich.
exercises.why: The negated statement at the end corrects what the first clause suggested.

exercises.english: The solution was not elegant, yet it worked.
exercises.german: Die Lösung war nicht elegant, sie hat trotzdem funktioniert.
exercises.why: Two independent main clauses whose contrast is carried by the word order and intonation alone, with no conjunction.

exercises.english: We argued for a long time, nothing was decided.
exercises.german: Wir haben lange diskutiert, beschlossen wurde nichts.
exercises.why: The second clause is passive and nominative: the contrast is made by word order alone.

exercises.english: Barely any coffee, but three meetings a day.
exercises.german: Kaum Kaffee, dafür drei Meetings am Tag.
exercises.why: dafür is an adversative particle; the verb is left out of the second nominalised clause.

exercises.english: He has a fever, she is completely healthy.
exercises.german: Er hat Fieber, sie ist völlig gesund.
exercises.why: A parallel present-tense pair comparing two people, no linking word needed.

exercises.english: Where is the rest?
exercises.german: Wo bleibt der Rest?
exercises.why: A short elliptical question whose meaning is only clear from the context, a frequent contrastive move in dialogue.

exercises.english: Rain again? Rain again?
exercises.german: Wieder Regen? Schon wieder Regen?
exercises.why: Repetition of the question word marks exasperation, a purely sentence-level contrast.

exercises.english: First the draft, then we will discuss.
exercises.german: Zuerst der Entwurf, dann diskutieren wir.
exercises.why: The first imperative and the second main clause contrast the order of two steps.

exercises.english: He laughed, and nobody laughed with him.
exercises.german: Er lachte, und keiner lachte mit.
exercises.why: A coordinated second clause with an ellipsis of the verb gruppe; the contrast comes from keiner alone.

exercises.english: Done – and now to the food!
exercises.german: Fertig – und jetzt zum Essen!
exercises.why: A two-part sentence: a bare elliptical statement followed by an imperative pivot, no connector.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: We waited a long time, but the queue moved at last.
exercises.german: Wir haben zwar lange gewartet, doch die Schlange bewegte sich endlich.
exercises.why: zwar … doch inverts the main clause: the verb moves behind doch, the subject follows it.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: The file is small, yet it takes forever to open.
exercises.german: Die Datei ist zwar klein, doch das Öffnen dauert ewig.
exercises.why: With doch the main clause is inverted, so it reads as a short, emphatic reaction.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: She is certainly right, though nobody believes her.
exercises.german: Sie hat zwar recht, doch niemand glaubt ihr.
exercises.why: Inverted main clause: the subject follows the verb, which is a hallmark of doch.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: The flat is fine, but there is no lift.
exercises.german: Die Wohnung ist in Ordnung, einen Aufzug gibt es dort jedoch nicht.
exercises.why: zwar can stand in field II as well; here the following clause ends with a negation that reverses it.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: Admittedly the app is useful, but it collects far too much data.
exercises.german: Zugegebenermaßen ist die App nützlich, sie sammelt aber viel zu viele Daten.
exercises.why: zugegebenermaßen concedes at the start of the sentence in a neutral, written register.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: It is admittedly a small point, but it changes the whole argument.
exercises.german: Zugegeben ist es ein kleiner Punkt, doch er ändert das ganze Argument.
exercises.why: The bare form zugegeben works as a sentence-initial concession, with doch inverting the main clause.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: His presentation was not exactly brilliant, but he got the job.
exercises.german: Sein Vortrag war na gut, er bekam die Stelle aber trotzdem.
exercises.why: na gut is the colloquial concession; the adverb placement in the main clause adds ironic understatement.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: The attempt was pretty useless, but we learned a lot.
exercises.german: Der Versuch war na gut nutzlos, wir haben aber viel daraus gelernt.
exercises.why: na gut in field I downgrades what follows, and the main clause recovers the value.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: The grammar exercise was not exactly easy, but it helped me a lot.
exercises.german: Die Grammatikübung war na nicht leicht, sie hat mir aber sehr geholfen.
exercises.why: na combines with a negation to concede in an understated, conversational way.

exercises.skill: Concession short: zwar ... aber / doch, zugegeben, na gut
exercises.english: The course is not cheap, but the material is worth the money.
exercises.german: Der Kurs ist na teuer, das Material ist aber jeden Cent wert.
exercises.why: na vor dem Komparativ is a spoken alternative to the written zugegebenermaßen.

exercises.english: Your shirt is blue, mine is white.
exercises.german: Dein Hemd ist blau, meins ist weiß.
exercises.why: Two main clauses set side by side; the second pronoun subject plus meins replaces the repeated noun.

exercises.english: He arrived on time, she ten minutes late.
exercises.german: Er kam pünktlich, sie zehn Minuten zu spät.
exercises.why: The second clause leaves out the verb; subject and adverbial alone carry the contrast.

exercises.english: Are you coming with us, or are you staying here?
exercises.german: Kommst du mit, oder bleibst du hier?
exercises.why: An either-or question is a contrast between two alternatives with no connector at all.

exercises.english: The children wanted to stay, the parents insisted on leaving.
exercises.german: Die Kinder wollten bleiben, die Eltern bestanden darauf zu fahren.
exercises.why: Two finite clauses with the verb repeated show the two camps set against each other.

exercises.english: I ordered coffee, she ordered tea.
exercises.german: Ich habe Kaffee bestellt, sie Tee.
exercises.why: The verb and the article are dropped in the second clause, so the ellipsis itself marks the contrast.

exercises.english: Of course nobody agrees, then who paid the deposit?
exercises.german: Natürlich stimmt niemand zu, und wer hat dann die Anzahlung gemacht?
exercises.why: The first clause is a negative statement, the second an impatient question about the same matter.

exercises.english: What a shame! And after all that work?
exercises.german: Schade! Und nach all der Arbeit?
exercises.why: An exclamation plus an elliptical question fragment; the missing verb heightens the reproach.

exercises.english: He is not stupid, just inexperienced.
exercises.german: Er ist nicht dumm, nur unerfahren.
exercises.why: The two predicative adjectives are contrasted by nur, which is a one-word contrastive adverb.

exercises.english: It was the plan that was wrong, not the team.
exercises.german: Der Plan war falsch, nicht das Team.
exercises.why: The negated part is moved to the end as a focus correction, with no connector in front of it.

exercises.english: Go ahead, just take an umbrella with you.
exercises.german: Mach ruhig, nimm nur einen Schirm mit.
exercises.why: The imperative concedes and then corrects with the particle nur, which is a contrastive adverb in field I of the second clause.
